note: Reference for the views of the Obsidian graph. The truth lives here and in the list of projects in _system/config.json; .obsidian/graph.json and .obsidian/bookmarks.json are brought up to date from this file with _system/scripts/apply_views.py (colors, default filter and one bookmark per view), only with Obsidian closed. A new project gets its color and its view by itself. In a query, {history} stands for every history type of config.json and {not_history} for the same, negated. This file holds folder names: it is the one place that differs per language.

layer_colors.name: History
layer_colors.paints: logs, inboxes, pending, decisions and reviews: what happened

layer_colors.name: System and listings
layer_colors.paints: rules, templates, root pages and generated listings

views.title: 0 Whole brain
views.shows: Every page, no filter, colored by layer. The default view.

views.title: 1 Clean map
views.shows: The brain without history, generated listings, system, raw sources or principles.

views.title: 2 Shared core
views.shows: The knowledge, without the detail of principles.

views.title: 3 One project and the core
views.shows: One view per project of config.json (parked ones aside): its live pages next to the summarized core. The query comes from project_view.

views.title: 4 History only
views.shows: Logs, decisions, reviews and inboxes, hanging from the cover of their project.
